failure_outcome: accepted residual N17: P1 restores carry no cross-domain terms, so with the other domain corrupt / UNKNOWN a trusted restore writes 256-261 over a possibly-existing (UNKNOWN) or, with a ghost, genuine obligation (write direction: the restoring domain's own verified ORIGINAL)
notes: F-PB01-2, DUPLICATE of F-FW05-2 (its UNKNOWN form), signature restore-over-corrupt-holder; sibling F-FW03-1. Severity: low: an ownership-integrity (R1 policy) residual, not a hazardous write: the restoring domain writes its own verified ORIGINAL; in the single-fault form the other domain holds no obligation (UNKNOWN only), so the bank ends at the owner's ORIGINAL and Dump stays visibly UNKNOWN-locked ('do NOT reboot'); overwriting a genuine obligation needs a second independent fault (a PR41-GHOST phantom: START refuses while the other snapshot is valid). Reachability: INFERRED: a PER-KEY boot load failure of the other domain's marker on a stored key (READ_ERROR when the length probe succeeds but the data read fails, or WRONG_SIZE / MALFORMED) while this domain holds a lease across the reboot; a whole-NVS failure makes both domains UNKNOWN and nothing is written; rate UNKNOWN. The Dump marker key holds CLEAR from the first lease, so the boot READ_ERROR is on a stored key (the firmware's length probe reports ABSENT for a key never stored). The bank ends at the owner's ORIGINAL. MODEL: boot fault read_error. Synthetic values only.
ownership: one dongle; Free Power and Dump to Grid leases, register 244 and the manual TOU owner domains as the firmware defines them; the synthetic SITE is the owner's ORIGINAL; an owner change outside any lease is the new ORIGINAL, a change while a domain holds the register is foreign (excluded until ECCO rewrites it)
smallest_safe_repair_scope: none required: S4 records N17 as an accepted residual. A bare '!other_corrupt' term is NOT a safe standalone change: the gate is the wrapper restore_free_power_snapshot (not the dispatch), shared by the automatic watchdog (P1) and the owner's End (P2, always admissible per S4); the term would strand the live grid-charge override (FP) or leave 244 = 0 uncontained (Dump) until an operator resolves the other domain (FW-03 / FW-05 mutants). The root cause is the boot arbitration being skipped when either side is corrupt; any R1 enforcement belongs to the boot lockout under an owner decision. Description only
